title: Juicy Algerian Celeriac Tagine
description: A rich, aromatic Algerian stew featuring celeriac, inspired by the flavors of a Buddhist temple. This dish is suitable for vegetarians and can be adapted for vegans.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large clay or ceramic tagine or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the chopped celeriac, cumin, coriander, paprika, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the chopped dried apricots and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Add the vegetable broth and bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and cook, covered, for 20-25 minutes, or until the celeriac is tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and bonito flakes, if using.
Serve warm, either on its own or over couscous or rice.
Optional: for a vegan version, omit the bonito flakes and use a vegan broth.
For a gluten-free version, be sure to use a gluten-free broth and check the ingredients of the cumin and coriander.
This dish is best made in advance and refrigerated or frozen for later use.
